newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall on profit-taking, foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall on profit-taking, foreign sales.

text.p: Increased sales by foreign firms and profit-taking by speculators drove share prices to a lower close on the Delhi Stock Exchange, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index ended 6.58 points lower at 633.06.
Traders said scattered buying by domestic financial institutions failed to arrest the fall in share prices.
"All round selling, mainly by foreign financial institutions (FIIs), pushed share prices down," said Harjit Thakur of brokers J.S. Chadha and Associates.
Cement maker ACC led the fall, dropping 36.40 rupees to 937.05 on heavy selling by FIIs, brokers said.
State Bank of India lost 7.35 rupees to 210.05.
Larsen and Toubro dropped 6.05 rupees to 205.45.
Hindustan Lever quoted 9.0 rupees lower at 780.0.
